name: Two-spotted spider mites
summary: Sap-feeding mites cause fine stippling from the leaf underside and visible webbing as populations increase.
indicators: Visible mites or eggs under magnification
exclusions: Silver scraped streaks with black specks
No organisms after careful underside inspection

progression.description: Fine pale stippling appears on individual leaves.
Bronzing spreads and mites or eggs are visible below.
Webbing spans leaves or flowers and plants decline.

confirmation: Look for round eggs and moving mites.
immediateActions: Inspect nearby plants and remove heavily infested material safely.
correctivePlan: Use a legal crop- and stage-appropriate IPM rotation.
warnings: Avoid spraying unsuitable products on flowers.
Webbing indicates an established population, not an early case.

sources.title: Spider Mites
sources.organization: University of California Statewide IPM Program
supportedClaims: Spider-mite feeding causes stippling and established populations can produce webbing; leaf-underside inspection is required.
